title: French's old horn and no longer playing
summary: Talk of how long since French played, his Supertone Bandmaster horn, trying to sell it, and a dental device for playing.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Me? How long ago you quit playing?

Me? How long ago? Oh, I'm a little. You know? Yeah, I got some teaching, I'm a teaching, I'm a teaching, I'm a teaching, I'm a teaching, I had to build one by one I like to take a look at it. Could we take a look at it?
Supertoned Bandmaster. Made in Elkhart, Indiana. I got that one out on the road. What other kind of horns have you had?
I had old, corn. I had a warm out. I wore many them things.
Pretty good on. A little oil. It's light too. It's not heavy.
You know the youngsters trying to like it? You are. See, I see none of these kids around here trying to play now?
No, none of them don't. I tried to sell it. They wouldn't buy it. I tried to sell it. I bought it. I bought it on the bar. Say that.
Wait, and then where are you waiting around? You ought to keep that and you ought to come back. Be nice to make some records.
Yeah, I'd say it'd be nice to make some records with you. Maybe we can do it someday. I'll work out good.

If I could fill it. You know what you tell me? If I could fill it, I'd choke them down there. But listen, the tempi they're making something now. It's not teethers, but it's fit over. Just like teethers. And you can put it in like you play a horn and play it just like you used to play it. And you can take it out when you get through. I wish I know how to get in my business or not. That's what that means.
Yeah, I heard about that. When he get it, you write and let me know about it.
Somebody was telling me about that some guy, two, three guys in California, all their teeth out, and they put their finger in the mouth and play the same way.
